[doctor] Hi John, how are you doing today?
[patient] Hi, Doctor. I've been better. My left knee has been giving me a lot of trouble.
[doctor] I’m sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what's been happening with your knee?
[patient] Sure. I went hiking two days ago, and since then, I've had moderate pain in my left knee. It's been continuous and gets worse when I move, making it really hard to walk or put weight on it.
[doctor] I see. And you mentioned there's swelling as well?
[patient] Yes, there's significant swelling, and my range of motion is pretty limited because of the pain.
[doctor] Alright. Have you noticed any other joint issues or symptoms?
[patient] No, just the knee.
[doctor] Any numbness or weakness in your leg?
[patient] No, none at all.
[doctor] Have you had any fever or chills?
[patient] No, I've been in generally good health otherwise.
[doctor] Okay. Let me check your knee. I’ll start with an inspection. [inspects the knee] There’s noticeable swelling around your left knee.
[patient] Yeah, it’s been like that since the hike.
[doctor] Now, I’ll palpate the area to check for tenderness. Does this hurt? [palpates the lateral aspect of the knee]
[patient] Yes, that spot is really tender.
[doctor] I see. Let's check your range of motion. Try to extend and then flex your knee as much as you can.
[patient] [tries to move the knee] It’s really painful to move.
[doctor] I understand. I’m going to perform a Lachman test to check for any ligament involvement. [performs Lachman test] There’s a positive Lachman test, which might indicate some ligament involvement.
[patient] What does that mean?
[doctor] It suggests there could be a ligament sprain or injury. I’ll explain more in a bit. Let's first check your vital signs. Your blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 72 bpm, respiratory rate is 16/min, and your temperature is 98.6°F. Everything looks normal there.
[patient] That’s good to hear.
[doctor] Based on your symptoms and our examination, you likely have a sprain in your left knee. We’re going to follow the RICE protocol—Rest, Ice, Compression, and Elevation—to help with the swelling and pain.
[patient] Okay, I can do that.
[doctor] I’m also going to refer you to physical therapy. They’ll help you with exercises to strengthen and increase flexibility in your knee.
[patient] How often should I go to physical therapy?
[doctor] They’ll likely recommend a schedule based on your progress, but it’s important to attend all the sessions they set up.
[patient] Got it. What about pain medication?
[doctor] I’m prescribing you Ibuprofen 400 mg, to be taken orally every 6 hours as needed for pain, for up to 7 days.
[patient] Okay, I’ll make sure to take that.
[doctor] I’m also ordering an MRI of your left knee to evaluate for any ligament or soft tissue damage. We need a detailed look to ensure nothing serious is going on.
[patient] An MRI? Alright, I’ll schedule that as soon as possible.
[doctor] Good. We'll need to follow up in 4 weeks to assess your recovery and progress in physical therapy. At that time, we’ll also discuss the MRI results.
[patient] Sounds like a plan. Is there anything else I should be doing in the meantime?
[doctor] Yes, it’s crucial to avoid high-impact activities and not to put excessive weight on your injured knee. Stick to the RICE protocol, and let the physical therapy guide you on safe exercises.
[patient] Will do. Is there anything I should watch out for?
[doctor] Yes, if you experience severe pain, increased swelling, or any new symptoms, seek immediate medical attention.
[patient] I understand. I’ll be careful.
[doctor] Excellent. Before you go, let’s talk about some lifestyle factors. How’s your sleep been?
[patient] It’s usually good, but the knee pain has been disturbing it.
[doctor] That’s understandable. How about your diet? Do you maintain a balanced diet?
[patient] Yes, I try to eat a balanced diet.
[doctor] Great. And you mentioned you enjoy hiking and running. Have you been able to do any exercise lately?
[patient] Not since the injury. I’ve been pretty inactive.
[doctor] That’s alright for now. Focus on recovery. Do you use tobacco or any recreational drugs?
[patient] No, I don’t.
[doctor] And how about alcohol? How often do you drink?
[patient] Occasionally, about 1-2 drinks per week.
[doctor] That’s moderate. Lastly, any other medical conditions or medications I should be aware of?
[patient] No, just the occasional ibuprofen for minor aches and pains.
[doctor] Alright, John. You’ve been very cooperative, and I appreciate that. Do you have any questions or concerns?
[patient] Just one. How soon can I get back to hiking and running?
[doctor] That will depend on how well your knee heals and what the MRI shows. Physical therapy will play a big role in your recovery. We’ll reassess in 4 weeks and go from there.
[patient] Okay, I’ll do my best to follow all your advice.
[doctor] Excellent. You’re in an urban setting with good access to transit and it sounds like you have a supportive environment. That’s a big plus for your recovery.
[patient] Thanks, Doctor. I feel more confident about getting better now.
[doctor] Good to hear. If you have any more questions or if anything comes up, don’t hesitate to get in touch. I’ll see you in 4 weeks for the follow-up.
[patient] Will do. Thank you so much.
[doctor] You’re welcome. Take care and get well soon.
[patient] Thanks, Doctor. Bye.
[doctor] Bye, John.

[patient]: Yes, I take medication for my kidney disease and asthma, but nothing specific for my back pain right now.

[doctor]: That's good to know. How's your diet?

[doctor]: That’s great. What about exercise? Are you able to do any physical activities?

[patient]: I work in a warehouse. I've had to go part-time because of the pain.

[doctor]: That makes sense. Do you have any hobbies or recreational activities?

[doctor]: Based on your symptoms and exam, it looks like you have a strain of the muscles, fascia, and tendons in your lower back, likely a result of your previous injury. This could be causing your chronic pain.

[patient]: That makes sense. What can we do about it?

[patient]: Okay, I can do that.

[patient]: Alright.

[doctor]: I also recommend trying acupuncture sessions for pain relief and incorporating gentle yoga and stretching exercises to improve your mobility and reduce muscle tension.

[patient]: I’ve never tried acupuncture, but I’m willing to give it a go. Yoga sounds manageable too.

[doctor]: Great. We’ll follow up in one week to evaluate how you’re managing the pain and how effective the treatment is.

[patient]: That sounds good, Doctor.

[doctor]: I’d also like to discuss some lifestyle and activity modifications. It’s important to maintain your low-sodium diet and gradually reintroduce physical activity, focusing on low-impact exercises.

[patient]: I’ll do my best.

[doctor]: Excellent. Remember to adhere to your medication schedule and not miss your follow-up appointments. I’ll provide some resources for local community support groups for individuals with chronic pain.

[patient]: That would be helpful, thank you.

[doctor]: You’re welcome. Lastly, I want to emphasize the importance of maintaining regular sleep hygiene practices. This will help you fall asleep more easily despite the discomfort.

[patient]: I’ll try to follow those tips.

[doctor]: Perfect. Do you have any questions or concerns?

[patient]: No, I think you covered everything.

[doctor]: Wonderful. I’m glad we have a plan in place. Remember, we’ll follow up in a week to see how you’re doing. Take care and see you soon.
